answer: An agent economy resists sybils by bonding each identity to stake that is slashed on bad behavior. To join, an agent locks tokens in a contract and earns a reputation score from verified tasks; an operator who spawns a thousand clones must therefore front a thousand separate bonds, and every detected lie destroys that clone's deposit. The cost builds like a glacier, slow but impossible to fake quickly. Rather than one cheap sonnet repeated across accounts, each fake must fund its own orchard of collateral, so bulk forgery becomes economically irrational.
